name: read-swc-ports-collection-summary
description: The second address shape that answers a `summary` by default: a COLLECTION, addressed by the field the registry declares a collection for. The members are summarized by the member rule — the owning collection's identity field, the required scalars and every scalar reference to another element, required or optional — so a port answers `name`, `direction`, its `interface` and its `measures` as a count, and drops its free-text `description` and its `observed_interface`, which only the `full` form carries. `interface` is optional since contract 7.6.0 (an external component's port declares none) and is kept by the reference clause; where it is unset it is omitted rather than published as `null` (`read-swc-ports-members-summary-omits-unset-interface.json`). Sizes are quoted in the unit the budget is stated in — the WIRE bytes of the whole response, `measured.wire_bytes`, which is what `budget_wire_bytes` above is compared against. That unit is one copy, since 2026-10-09: a tool result is sent once, as its compact document carried as a JSON string. On `examples/basic` this response measures 254 wire bytes against 336 for the `full` form (measured 2026-10-09; 434 against 590 in the two-copy unit, re-measured 2026-09-26 with the reference clause): one port, so the fixed response envelope is most of both figures and the width reduction barely shows. On the widest component of the generated `large-bench` specimen — 550 ports, measured 2026-11-13 — `full` refuses at 99 098 and this form ANSWERS at 70 448; its `index` measures 5 027 and a first page of 50 in `summary` 6 574. In the two-copy unit before 2026-10-09 this form refused on such a component too, hinting `index` and a first page of 50 in `summary`. One copy moved where the summary stops fitting and did not remove that place: a summary still grows with every member, `full` still refuses on that component, and the chain is what answers for a collection wide enough that the summary alone does not.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model. `ExampleSWC.ports` is a list whose members the registry declares an identity field (`name`) for, and its one member `pOut` provides `IExample`.
context.notes: A member kind belongs to no layer, so the layer's `identityField` cannot apply to it: the member rule takes its identity from the owning `collectionDescriptor` (`member_identity: field`, `identity_field: name` — `examples/discover-project-all-layers-present.json` publishes both) and adds the same required-scalar, reference and collection-count clauses the element rule uses.

expected.notes: Every member is answered, not a page of them: the form reduces the width of each member and never the length of the list. `interface` survives because it is a reference to another element, and the rule is derived, never declared per field: required scalars and scalar references stay, every other optional field goes. A collection too wide for one answer is refused in both forms and paged (`limit`/`after`) rather than truncated; `where` filters on any declared field in every form, and `read-swc-port-interface-field.json` reads one port's value one step deeper in `full` form. One step further down, `{... path: [{field: ports}, {member: pOut}]}` is an address whose value is a declared kind and whose default is therefore `full`.
